reader.notes: Same mechanism as the alternate key: one byte window in the shared record area. Every verb tried through a record other than the key's own selected the right record.

refuter.evidence: Same probe kov-003 (src/kov.cob): REC-C describes the prime key window 1-4 as PIC S9(7) PACKED-DECIMAL while the key is described only in REC-A as X(4). W4 02 (packed +5 written through REC-C), W5 IK 22 (same packed +5 again, a different alternate key: prime duplicate refused), R2 00 +0000005 CCC1 TAILC1 (READ KEY IS KEY-A with the bytes saved from KEY-A after the REC-C write finds it), and the packed-keyed record sorts first in ascending prime order as N2 shows.
